title.narrative: World Bank Umbrella Facility for Trade

description.narrative: Australia's contribution to the World Bank Umbrella Facility for Trade supports economic recovery from Covid-19 through trade. It supports developing countries in the Indo-Pacific to align their trade practices with the WTO Trade Facilitation Agreement, helping identify constraints to cross-border trade, supporting reforms, and helping increase the predictability, transparency, and harmonisation of customs procedures and transit standards. The investment also supports developing countries to participate in digital trade by assisting them to develop policy and regulatory frameworks conducive to digital trade and supports participation in the WTO Joint Statement Initiative on E-commerce.

title.narrative: Stocktaking/Assessment & Learning Review of the Trade Facilitation Support Programme

description.narrative:
Advancing inclusive trade in the Pacific
Australia’s long-standing Aid for Trade partnerships with the World Bank Trade Facilitation Support Program (TSFP) and Pacific Islands Forum (PIF) Secretariat supported the development and launch of the Pacific Regional Trade Facilitation Strategy at the Global Aid for Trade Review in Geneva in June 2024. The result of several year’s of work by the TSFP and PIF Secretariat, the Strategy is an important milestone under the Pacific Aid for Trade Strategy. It specifies regional approaches that can support national trade facilitation reforms, including support to implement the WTO Trade Facilitation Agreement and Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations Plus. Australia continues to support PIF Members to address challenges identified in the Strategy, such as inefficient border procedures, excessive documentation requirements, and opaque controls that undermine trade flows and hinder regional economic growth and integration. The Strategy represents years of collaboration between partners and demonstrates a commitment to cooperate and collaborate to address trade barriers and deliver economic resilience and prosperity across the region.

Multi-year advisory support was provided to Timor-Leste to establish its Trade Information Portal (TIP), which was officially launched in April 2024. The TIP is a web-based system that provides a single source for all cross-border regulatory trade information. Over 165 laws, regulations, procedures, and other trade-related measures from 22 different government agencies are now accessible online. Businesses can also find licenses, permits, and applicable fees through the portal. The portal aims to ensure import and export processes and procedures are more transparent and predictable. The portal reinforces the country’s efforts to integrate into regional and global markets and aligns with relevant provisions of the WTO TFA and ASEAN ATIGA.

Through the World Bank’s global Umbrella Facility for Trade (UFT), Australia supports technical assistance and capacity building in the areas of trade facilitation, digital trade and e-commerce, with a focus on assisting developing and least developed countries in our region. Our commitment to the UFT's Trade Facilitation Support Program (TFSP) supported developing country World Trade Organization (WTO) Members to implement their obligations under the WTO's Agreement on Trade Facilitation to streamline and simplify trade procedures, making it faster, cheaper, and easier to import and export goods. For example, during the reporting period the TFSP facilitated analysis of operations at the Cambodia-Thai Stueng Bot border post by Cambodian and Thai officials, private sector actors, and contractors. Participants made a range of recommendations to advance and streamline the initiative.

Through the World Bank’s global Umbrella Facility for Trade (UFT), Australia supports technical assistance and capacity building in the areas of trade facilitation, digital trade and e-commerce, with a focus on assisting developing and least developed countries in our region. Our support helped the UFT deliver its Trade Facilitation Support Program (TFSP) in Timor-Leste, newly acceded to the World Trade Organization (WTO). The TSFP provided capacity building assistance to Timor-Leste on its new obligations under the WTO's Agreement on Trade Facilitation (TFA), undertook a gap analysis and developed a roadmap for TFA implementation, and helped Timor-Leste to integrate these requirements into its national trade policy. Timor-Leste is now better positioned to benefit from global and regional trade opportunities and partnerships, including in the context of its accession to the Association of Southeast Asian Nations.

Through the World Bank’s global Umbrella Facility for Trade (UFT), Australia supports technical assistance and capacity building in the areas of trade facilitation, digital trade and e-commerce, with a focus on assisting developing and least developed countries in our region. The UFT's Digital Advisory and Trade Assistance Fund assisted the Philippines Government to analyse and develop its Konektadong Pinoy Act, enacted in July 2025. The Act is a major step in the Philippines' implementation of the World Trade Organization's General Agreement on Trade in Services, the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership and the ASEAN-Australia-New Zealand Free Trade Agreement. This work is expected to help create a regulatory environment that encourages fair competition and investment in digital infrastructure, modernising and enhancing opportunities for Philippine businesses to engage effectively in e-commerce and digital trade.

Through the World Bank’s global Umbrella Facility for Trade (UFT), Australia supports technical assistance and capacity building in the areas of trade facilitation, digital trade and e-commerce, with a focus on assisting developing and least developed countries in our region. The UFT's Digital Advisory and Trade Assistance Fund supported Fiji to advance a national e-commerce strategy for data protection that will boost exports of business services from Fiji. This included working with Fiji’s Digital Transformation Office to support the Fiji Data Protection Act 2025 and adopt a National Data Protection and Privacy Policy. Implementation of this framework, which aligns with international data protection standards, ensures Fiji services providers can meet Australian requirements, thereby boosting the number of Fijian outsourcing services available to Australian businesses.
